hook_text: One crane idea is a guess. Two is a choice. Fold the page and draw them both before you cut a single piece of card.
clip_script: Fold the page. Left side: a tall mast with an arm that swings round it, load up, arm turns, load drops in the bin. Right side: an arm hinged at the bottom that tips up like a seesaw. Two different cranes, not one crane in two colours. Label everything: base, mast, hinge, string, magnet, counterweight, and what each is made of. Now tick them against the brief. Lifts 150 millimetres? Swings 200? Stands up loaded? The crosses choose for you. Then the circuit: cell, push switch, coil, bulb, one loop, four symbols, ruler, square corners, switch drawn open. Press and the bulb says the magnet is on. That is a design on paper, and paper is the cheapest place to make mistakes.
visual_style: Whiteboard page folding; two crane silhouettes appearing with arrows for movement; labels popping in; a four-symbol circuit rectangle drawn with a ruler.
mood: Decisive and encouraging, a designer thinking aloud.
pacing: Fold, left, right, labels, ticks, circuit, each beat a few seconds.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch two cranes of your own.
